documents.title: Home Services Application (initial, renewal and change of ownership). The page titled "Required documentation to be provided with this application" lists the initial-applicant policy checklist.
documents.issuer: Illinois Department of Public Health, Health Care Facilities and Programs Section
documents.version: The form footer reads 'Updated 8/9/2023' on pp. 1-5 and 'Updated 6/8/2023' on pp. 6-8. The file posted on the IDPH site is named hs-application-092024.pdf.
documents.how_used: This is the main document. No single policy-review checklist exists apart from the application, so the 'Initial Applicants ONLY' checklist on page 8 is the item list, with the document's own regulatory cites as item IDs. Application-only items are excluded: forms, ownership, governing-body officers, revenue sources, client counts, geographic area, employee roster, manager qualification form (Attachment E), affidavits, fee, proof of liability coverage (245.90 a) 2)) and proof of Health Care Worker Registry access (955.115).

documents.title: Home Health, Home Services, and Home Nursing Agency Code, 77 Ill. Adm. Code 245 (Sections 245.30, 245.40, 245.90 and 245.210)
documents.issuer: Illinois Department of Public Health (published by JCAR)
documents.version: Current codified text on the ILGA/JCAR site. Section 245.30(c) shown here is the version cited in the search results (Section 245.40 history notes an amendment effective Nov. 8, 2023).
documents.how_used: This supports the application checklist. <cite index="33-4">Section 245.90(a)(3)(I) requires copies of policies and procedures with the initial application, starting with complaint resolution (245.30(b)(3)) and employee health and safety (245.30(c)(1)(H) and (I)).</cite> <cite index="33-5,33-7,33-8">It also requires client service contracts (245.220), acceptance criteria (245.210(d)) and sample service plan forms (245.210(e)).</cite> I could not open the full regulation text directly; the ilga.gov pages returned permission errors. The wording of regulation items below comes from search excerpts.

documents.title: Surveillance Nurse Visit Checklist (Home Services)
documents.how_used: Used only to show how the policy manual is reviewed at survey. It lists policy and procedure manuals, bylaws, governing body minutes, complaint log and process, training files, job descriptions, service plan, and Alzheimer's/dementia training curriculum. These are not added as required policy items.

required_items.text: A copy of the current client contract per 245.220 for Home Services, plus any attachments noted in the contract (e.g., rights and responsibilities, service plan, rate sheet).
A copy of your scope of services.
Initial applicants only: copy of job description for all positions.
Initial applicants only: complaint resolution policy.
Initial applicants only: employee health and safety policy. Section 245.90(a)(3)(I)(ii) cites both 245.30(c)(1)(H) and (I) for this policy.
Initial applicants only: infection control policy.
Initial applicants only: health care worker background check process.
Initial applicants only: supervisory visit for client policy.
Initial applicants only: supervisory visit for home service worker policy.
required_items.cite: IDPH Form 445104, p. 8 (245.40 c) 6 B i - iii))

required_items.text: Initial applicants only: client records management and release requirements.
Initial applicants only: employee training procedures.
Initial applicants only: acceptance of client policy. <cite index="16-5">The regulation says home services agencies shall develop and follow policies on acceptance and discharge of clients.</cite>
Initial applicants only: sample service plan form.

Personnel policies, available to all full- and part-time employees: wage scales, benefits, hours of work and leave time. These are regulation content not listed separately on the application checklist.
Personnel policies: requirements for an initial health evaluation of each new employee (or placed worker) who has contact with clients, as specified by the governing body.
Personnel policies: orientation to the agency and appropriate continuing education.
Personnel policies: job descriptions for all positions used by the agency.

Personnel policies: employee health policies requiring employees to report health symptoms and exposure to communicable or infectious disease, and specifying when employees are removed from and may resume client contact.
Personnel policies: agency procedures for identifying potential dangers to the health and safety of personnel providing services in the home, and for protecting them from those dangers.

sections: Required documentation (all applicants): client contract per 245.220 with attachments; scope of services; fee schedule

Initial Applicants ONLY: job descriptions; proof of liability coverage; complaint resolution policy; employee health and safety policy; infection control policy; health care worker background check process; supervisory visit for client policy; supervisory visit for home service worker policy; client records management and release; employee training procedures; acceptance of client policy; sample service plan form; proof of Health Care Worker Registry access

notes: The application has no numbered items. It uses a bulleted checklist, and each line carries a regulatory cite in parentheses, which I used as the item ID. The policies are due with an initial application, mailed to IDPH with the $1,500 fee (the form says electronic submission is not accepted). The checklist does not require the manual to follow any set order or category scheme, so mirroring the checklist order is a sensible way to organize it. IDPH surveyors later ask to see the 'Policy and Procedure Manuals' (surveillance checklist). I left out these checklist lines as non-policy paperwork: proof of general liability coverage ($1M per occurrence / $3M aggregate, 245.90(a)(2)), proof of Health Care Worker Registry access (955.115), and the Attachment E manager qualification form. The fee schedule is also not listed as a policy item. Gaps: (1) The full text of 245.30(c)(1)(E)-(G), 245.40(c) and 245.210(e)-(h) was not retrievable in full, so I did not list items I could not confirm. Check the full Part 245 text on the JCAR site for those. (2) The application's checklist cites only 245.30(c)(1)(I) for employee health and safety, while 245.90(a)(3)(I)(ii) cites both (H) and (I), so cover both. (3) For Alzheimer's/dementia training, see 245.211 and 77 Ill. Adm. Code 973, which the surveillance checklist asks for. This is a training curriculum, not a policy checklist item. (4) Agencies serving only CCP, DHS-DRS or VA clients may be excluded from IDPH licensure (245.20), and the application's client counts exclude those clients.
